choices.title: Herd immunity

• Herd immunity is a form of indirect protection from infectious disease that occurs when a large percentage of a population has become immune to an infection thereby providing a measure of protection for individuals who are not immune.   • Passive immunity is the transfer of active humoral immunity of ready-made antibodies. Passive immunity can occur naturally, when maternal antibodies are transferred to the fetus through the placenta, and it can also be induced artificially, when high levels of antibodies specific to a pathogen or toxin (obtained from humans, horses, or other animals) are transferred to non-immune persons through blood products that contain antibodies, such as in immunoglobulin therapy or antiserum therapy.
  • Active immunity is the one that develops after exposure to a disease-causing infectious microorganism or other foreign substance, such as following infection or vaccination.
  • Contact immunity is the property of some vaccines, where a vaccinated individual can confer immunity upon unimmunized individuals through contact with bodily fluids or excrement.

During prenatal development, the umbilical cord is physiologically and genetically part of the fetus and normally contains two arteries and one vein. It is buried within Wharton’s jelly, a gelatinous substance largely made of mucopolysaccharides and acts as a mucous connective tissue. The umbilical vein supplies the fetus with oxygenated nutrient rich blood from the placenta.

• Induction of labor is defined as the process of artificially stimulating the uterus to start a labor. It is usually performed by administering oxytocin or prostaglandins or by manually rupturing the amniotic membranes because ruptured membranes are associated with a higher risk of neonatal infection than intact membranes, the induction of labor approximately 24 hours after women’s waters break.
  • Placenta previa is a condition wherein there is an abnormal placentation near or covering the internal os. Hence inducing labor and vaginal delivery is a complicated process.
  • Cephalopelvic disproportion occurs when fetal head is too large to fit through the mother’s pelvis. Hence inducing labor would not be a successful measure.
  • Cord prolapsed is a complication in which the umbilical cord prolapses through the open cervix into the vagina ahead of the fetus. Hence the cord gets trapped against the baby’s body and inducing labor would not be effective.
  • Premature rupture of membranes refers to a patient who is beyond 37 weeks gestation and presented with rupture of membranes prior to onset of labor.

• Electroconvulsive therapy or ECT involves unilateral or bilateral placement of electrodes over the non-dominant hemisphere of head to induce tonic-clonic seizures under sedation. It causes anticonvulsants effects, brain remodeling and improves brain perfusion. It is indicated for conditions such as refractory cases, life threatening symptoms or if medication is contraindicated in case of pregnancies. The common disorders that are managed by ECT are depression, schizoaffective disorder, schizophrenia with catatonia, bipolar mood disorder, highly suicidal or pregnant depressed patients and neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
  • With appropriate modifications, electroconvulsive therapy may be considered a treatment option even in the presence of clinical evidence of increased intracranial pressure.

• Health education is defined as the principle by which individuals and group of people, learn to behave in a manner conducive to the promotion, maintenance, or restoration of health. The principles of health education are:
    • Credibility: It is the degree to which the message to be communicated is perceived as trustworthy by the receiver.
    • Comprehension: It highlights that health educator must know the level of understanding, education and literacy of people to whom the teaching is directed.
    • Interest: It signifies that health education should be related to the interests of the people and should be based on felt needs so that it becomes people’s program.
    • Known to unknown: Health education should proceed from known to unknown that is the health communicator uses the existing knowledge of the people as hints on which to hang new knowledge.

choices.correct_explanation:
• Idiosyncratic reactions occur rarely and unpredictably in a small percentage of the population due to a response to a treatment or medicine. It usually occurs with exposure to new medicines and is not clear with the mechanism of action of the medicine. It can be either immune mediated manifested by skin rashes to systemic symptoms or it can be non-immune mediated related to abnormal production of cytotoxic metabolites.
  • Allergic reactions are usually caused due to interpretation of a foreign substance as allergen by a body and are manifested as inflammation, sneezing and coughing.
  • Toxic effects usually indicate adverse effects produced by poisons wherein the effects ranges from slight symptoms, such as headaches, nausea to severe symptoms such as coma, convulsions and death.
  • Side effects are typically undesirable effect of a drug or medical treatment.

choices.title: Independent variable
choices.correct_explanation:
• Experimental research is a study that strictly adheres to a scientific research design. It includes a hypothesis, a variable that can be manipulated by the researcher and variables that can be measured, calculated and compared.
  • Experimental manipulation describes the process by which researchers purposefully change, alter, or influence the independent variables (IVs), which are also called treatment variables or factors in an experimental research design. This process allows researchers to explore causal relationships between IVs and dependent variables (DVs), which are also referred to as outcome or criterion variables of interest in a particular study. Specifically, manipulation of an IV allows researchers to explore whether the IV causes change in a study’s DVs.
    • Example: If a researcher conducts an experiment to test the effect of a medicine on blood pressure of rats, then:
  • The independent variable is the amount of medicine being given to the rats within the experiment and it is controlled by the experimenting researcher.
  • The dependent variable being affected by the independent variable is the blood pressure.
  • Outcome variables are usually the dependent variables which are observed and measured by changing independent variables. These variables determine the effect of the cause (independent) variables when changed for different values.   
  • Criterion variable is a name used to describe the dependent variable in a variety of statistical modeling contexts, including multiple regression, discriminant analysis, and canonical correlation.

choices.title: Null hypothesis
choices.correct_explanation:
• A statistical hypothesis is an assumption about a population parameter. This assumption may or may not be true. In statistics, a hypothesis test calculates some quantity under a given assumption. The result of the test allows to interpret whether the assumption holds or whether the assumption has been violated. The assumption of a statistical test is called the null hypothesis or H0. It is often called the default assumption or the assumption that nothing has changed.
  • Directional hypothesis predicts the nature of the effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable.
  • Non-directional hypothesis predicts that the independent variable has an effect on the dependent variable, but the direction of the effect is not specified.
  • A research hypothesis is a specific, clear and testable proposition or predictive statement about the possible outcome of a scientific research study based on a particular property of a population, such as presumed differences between groups on a particular variable or relationships between variables.

The roundish brim encourages fetal rotation. The pubic arch is at 90 degrees or wider. Powerful uterine contractions are required to push the presenting part downwards.
  • Android pelvis has a heart-shaped brim and is quite narrow in front. The pelvic cavity and outlet are often narrow, straight and long. The ischial spines are prominent. Due to this shape of the pelvis, progressive difficulty is faced, rotation fails to occur and transverse arrest is common. Hence it’s important that such women take an active role during labor and need to squat and move around as much as possible.
  • Anthropoid pelvis has an oval brim and slightly narrow pelvic cavity. The outlet is large, although some of the other diameters may be reduced. If the baby engages in the pelvis in an anterior position, labor would be expected to be straightforward in most cases. 
  • The platypelloid pelvis has kidney-shaped brim and the pelvic cavity is usually shallow and may be narrow in the antero-posterior (front to back) diameter. The outlet is usually roomy. During labor the engagement of fetal head is difficult, but once in, there should be no further difficulty.

choices.title: Varying degrees of abdominal pain during ovulation
choices.correct_explanation:
• Mittelschmerz is one-sided, lower abdominal pain associated with ovulation. It occurs midway through a menstrual cycle about 14 days before the next menstrual period. It is usually caused due to stretching of the surface of the ovary because of the follicle growth just prior to an ovulation. The pain is one-sided, dull and cramp-like, sharp and sudden and it may or may not be accompanied by mild vaginal bleeding or discharge. It rarely requires any medical intervention unless and until the pain becomes severe and is accompanied by nausea or fever which could be an indicator for PID or ectopic disease.
  • Pelvic girdle pain in pregnancy is a collection of uncomfortable symptoms caused due to misalignment or stiffness of pelvic joints either at the back or front of pelvis. Pain is usually felt over the pubic bone at the front in the center, pain across one or both sides of lower back or over perineum. The pain aggravates during walking, going upstairs or turning over in bed.
  • Lower abdominal cramp during menstruation is known as dysmenorrhea. It is usually caused due to uterine contractions and can be mild or severe accompanied by nausea and vomiting.
  • Intermittent uterine contraction during labor is known as Braxton Hicks contraction which is infrequent, irregular and involves only cramping. The contractions occur only for 10 to 20 minutes and are also known as false labor.

choices.title: Vasa previa
choices.correct_explanation:
• Vasa previa is a condition in which the umbilical cord vessels cross or run near the internal opening of the uterus. It is usually found in conditions such as low-lying placenta or in vitro fertilization. The classic triad of vasa previa is membrane rupture, painless vaginal bleeding and fetal bradycardia or fetal death. The women with vasa previa deliver through elective Cesarean prior to rupture of membranes usually at 35 – 36 weeks.
  • Abruption placenta is defined as the premature separation of placenta from the uterus. It is one of the leading causes of third trimester bleeding associated with fetal and maternal morbidity and mortality. It is usually caused due to maternal hypertension, maternal trauma, short umbilical cord and sudden decompression of uterus. The mother manifests with vaginal bleeding, abdominal or back pain and uterine tenderness, fetal distress and abnormal uterine contractions. Cesarean delivery is often necessary for fetal and maternal stabilization. If hemorrhage cannot be controlled after delivery, a cesarean hysterectomy may be required to save the patient’s life.
  • Placenta accreta occurs when all or part of the placenta attaches abnormally to the myometrium of uterus. It results in increased risk of heavy bleeding at the time of attempted vaginal delivery. Maternal age, multipara mothers, prior uterine surgery, curettage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are the risk factors for this disorder.
  • Placenta previa, a condition in which the placenta partially or wholly blocks the neck of the uterus, so interfering with normal delivery of a baby.

choices.correct_explanation:
• Sequestration is a process of chemically blocking or sequestrating a substance. In patients with sickle cell disease the RBCs become stiff and shaped like a crescent or a sickle, and trap the blood vessels in the spleen. It leads to swelling and enlargement of spleen, wherein the clients manifest with severe pain, rapid drop in Hematocrit results in weakness, anemia, and rapid heart rate.
  • Pernicious anemia results from vitamin B12 deficiency. An autoimmune destruction of parietal cells leads to impaired intrinsic factor production thereby resulting in decreased absorption of adequate dietary vitamin B12.
  • Aplastic anemia is a syndrome of bone marrow failure characterized by peripheral pancytopenia and marrow hypoplasia. The causative factor is either congenital or inherited.
  • Iron deficiency anemia is a common type of anemia in which the body stores of iron drop too low to support normal red blood cell (RBC) production. It is usually caused due to inadequate dietary iron, impaired iron absorption, bleeding or loss of body iron in the urine.

choices.correct_explanation: • The foundation of research is the scientific method. It is a standardized way of making observations, gathering data, forming theories, testing predictions and interpreting results. choices.title: Population
choices.correct_explanation:
• Population is a complete set of elements (persons or objects) that possess some common characteristic defined by the sampling criteria established by the researcher. It is the entire group of people or objects to which the researcher wishes to generalize the study findings. Example: Elderly with Alzheimer
  • Group: In an experiment or study that does not receive treatment by the researchers and is then used as a benchmark to measure how the other tested subjects do.
  • Stratified sampling refers to a sampling method in which the total population is divided into non-overlapping subgroups. Each of the subgroups is called a stratum and two or more subgroups are called strata.
  • Sample is a group of people, objects or items that are taken from a larger population for measurement. It is a representative of population to ensure generalizing the findings from the research sample to the population as a whole.

choices.title: Chadwick sign
choices.correct_explanation:
• Chadwick’s sign is a bluish discoloration of the cervix, vagina and labia resulting from increased blood flow. It is usually found as early as 6 to 8 weeks after conception and is an early sign of pregnancy.
  • Hegar’s sign is a softening in the consistency of the uterus. It is usually present from 4 to 6 weeks until the 12th week of pregnancy. On bimanual examination, (two fingers in the anterior fornix and two fingers below the uterus per abdomen) the abdominal and vaginal fingers seem to oppose below the body of uterus (examination must be gentle to avoid abortion).
  • Goodell’s sign is an indication of pregnancy. It is a significant softening of the cervix from increased vascularization which is a result of hypertrophy and engorgement of the vessels below the growing uterus. It usually occurs at 4 weeks gestation.
  • Osiander’s sign is the presence of vaginal pulsation that mirrors the maternal heart rate as an early sign of pregnancy.

choices.title: Role play
choices.correct_explanation:
• Role playing is the changing of one’s behavior to assume a role, either unconsciously to fill a social role, or consciously to act out an adopted role. It is performed for amusement, entertainment, training or education purposes. It is even considered as an important part of psychological development. It results in behavioral change and change in attitude.
  • Puppetry or puppet show is a form of theatre or performance that involves the manipulation of puppets—inanimate objects, often resembling some type of human or animal figure, that are animated or manipulated by a human called a puppeteer. It helps in enhancing communication skills, understanding concepts of the learner, increases creative thinking and develops motor skills.
  • Group discussion is a child-centered strategy in which students are divided into groups and are encouraged to discuss on the subject matter given. This discussion is dominated by the teacher and most of the time teacher is active and student accepts his ideas and views. It improves listening, thinking as well as speaking skill of the student.
  • Symposium is a series of speeches on a selected subject. Each person or expert presents an aspect of subject briefly.  Simple aspects of the topic are discussed and the chairperson is responsible to control the speech. The more time is involved for discussion with participants.

choices.title: Intussusception
choices.correct_explanation:
• Intussusception is a medical condition in which a part of the intestine folds into a section immediately ahead of it. It usually involves the small intestine rather than large intestine. The cause is unknown but the disease usually arises in children due to infections, or anatomical defects or altered mobility. In the most common type of intussusceptions, the ileum enters the cecum which thereby leads to blood supply cut off which causes ischemia and the mucosa sloughs off into the gut. This creates the classically described red currant jelly stool which is a mixture of sloughed mucosa, blood and mucus. The other symptoms accompanying it are periodical abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, pulling legs to the chest area and intermittent abdominal cramps. Physical examination reveals a “sausage shaped” mass felt upon palpating the abdomen. The condition can be treated with either barium or water-soluble enema or by surgical reduction in case of failure of medical management.
  • Hirschsprung’s disease is a birth defect in which there is absence of nerve cells at the end of a child’s bowel. It results in abnormal movement of stool through the bowel. The child manifests with constipation or infrequent bowel movements, growth failure, unexplained fever and vomiting.  Child with this disorder does not respond to laxatives and is treated surgically.
  • Pyloric stenosis is an uncommon condition in infants that blocks food from entering the small intestine. The pylorus muscle of the stomach thickens and become abnormally large, blocking food from reaching the small intestine. This condition results in forceful vomiting, dehydration and weight loss.
  • Tracheoesophageal fistula is a congenital or acquired communication between the trachea and esophagus. The child manifests with frothy, white bubbles in the mouth, coughing or choking when feeding, vomiting, cyanosis, difficulty breathing and round and full abdomen.

choices.correct_explanation:
• Stomatitis is defined as the inflammation of the mucous membranes of the mouth. It is even referred as the pain or inflammation of the mucous membranes. It is relatively common side effect of chemotherapy and sometimes radiotherapy. It can even affect the inner lips, cheeks, gums, tongue and throat. It can even be caused due to some other infection, disease or even nutritional deficiency. Stomatitis is usually treated by topical corticosteroids, topical antibiotics and anesthetics.

Figure: Stomatitis

·         Gingivitis is defined as the inflammation of the gums or gingival, which commonly occurs because of accumulation of thin film of plaque on the teeth. It is usually a non-destructive type of periodontal disease, but untreated gingivitis can progress to periodontitis.

·         Glossitis refers to the inflammation of the tongue which leads to soreness, swollen and inflamed tongue. It is usually caused due to allergic reactions to oral care products, foods or medicine.

·         Cheilosis, also known as cheilitis, is a painful inflammation and cracking of the corners of the mouth either on one side or both the sides. It is usually found in people with ill-fitting dentures that fail to adequately separate the upper and lower jaws.

choices.correct_explanation:
• Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum. It is most commonly spread through sexual activity and may also be transmitted from mother to baby during pregnancy or at birth resulting in congenital syphilis. The signs and symptoms begin with a firm, painless, non-itchy skin ulceration, which later progresses to diffuse rashes involving the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. In the later stages there may be no symptoms and later it may progress to soft non-cancerous growth to vital systems of the body such as nerves, heart, etc.
  • Chlamydia trachomatis commonly called Chlamydium is a bacterium that causes Chlamydia, which can manifest in various ways including trachoma, lymphogranuloma venereum, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, salpingitis and pelvic inflammatory disease.
  • Cytomegalovirus is a common virus that affects babies if a mother is infected during pregnancy. It is spread through sexual and non-sexual contact with body secretions. It is a type of herpes virus and causes symptoms immediately after infection. The commonly affected organs are lungs, gastrointestinal tract, brain, spinal cord or eyes.
  • Human papillomavirus infection is caused by HPV. It is usually spread by sustained direct skin to skin contact and even spreads from mother to baby. In most of the cases it causes no symptoms and gets resolved within 2 years. However, in some it results in either warts or precancerous lesions.

choices.correct_explanation:
• Talipes equinus, or equinovarus or club foot, is a common foot abnormality in which the foot points downwards and inwards, that is there is plantar flexion of ankle and foot. It is usually caused due to various predisposing factors such as intrauterine compression in case of large baby, abnormally shaped or small uterus or abnormal intrauterine fluid levels. The intrinsic factors are rigid and small calf muscle which results in the abnormality. The peculiar signs are:
    • Stiff, rigid, foot of varying degrees
    • Short and/or tight Achilles tendon (heel cord), with foot pointing downward
    • The heel is turned in
    • Deep heel crease; soft, puffy heel pad; wide front foot area and overall smaller foot

• ABC analysis is a method of tiered inventory or supplier evaluation that divides inventory or suppliers into various categories based on cost per unit and quantity held in stock or turned over a period of time. It allows inventory or purchasing managers to segregate and manage the overall inventory or supplier management techniques to be applied to different segments of the inventory in order to increase revenue and decrease costs.

By paying close attention in real-time to the optimization of these items in inventory, a great positive impact is possible with minimal increase in inventory management costs.
  • “B” Category items represent 30%–35% of inventory items by item type and about 15% of the value. It is usually caused due to the obstruction of the bile flow from the gall bladder. The most common factor for biliary colic is presence of gall stones. A person with biliary colic usually complains of an ache or a feeling of pressure in the upper abdomen. The pain is usually in the upper right abdomen and may radiate to back towards the shoulder.
  • Midepigastric pain that radiates to back is found in patients with pancreatitis. It is inflammation of pancreas which can either be acute or chronic due to inadequate release of enzymes from the pancreas.

choices.correct_explanation: • Intracranial pressure (ICP) is the pressure exerted by fluids such as cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) inside the skull and on the brain tissue and it is measured in mmHg. At rest, the ICP is normally 5–15 mmHg for a supine adult. Any causes such as mass effect in case of brain tumor or generalized brain swelling, hypertensive encephalopathy, any obstruction to CSF flow or increased CSF production may increase ICP. Any occult leak of CSF into another body cavity as a result of lumbar puncture can cause decreased ICP. Hence the option 5–15 mmHg is the correct one.

·         The objectives of hemodialysis are to extract toxic nitrogenous substances from the blood and to remove excess water. In hemodialysis, the blood, loaded with toxins and nitrogenous wastes is diverted from the patient to a dialyzer, in which it’s cleaned and then returned to the patient.

  • Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common encapsulated Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium that can cause disease in plants and animals including humans. It is usually found in association with serious illness, especially in hospital.
  • Acinetobacter baumannii is a Gram-negative bacillus that is aerobic, pleomorphic and non-motile. It’s an opportunistic pathogen that affects individuals with prolonged hospital stay.

choices.title: Accountability
choices.correct_explanation:
• According to the code of ethics of ANA, accountability means to be answerable to oneself and others for one’s own actions. For example, 3 nurses noted that a client consistently refused to take his medication. Instead of addressing the issue of why the client was refusing his medication, the nurses threw it away and recorded that it had been administered. In this case nurses are accountable to advocate for their clients and are held accountable for their actions and decisions. The nurses should have explored solutions with the client and the health care team and also should have documented the issue and also the actions taken by the nurse.
  • Responsibility is defined as the obligation to perform duties, tasks or roles using sound professional judgement and being answerable for the decisions made in doing this.
  • Fidelity is keeping ones promises. The nurse must be faithful and true to their professional promises and responsibilities by providing high quality, safe care in a competent manner.
  • Veracity is being completely truthful with patients; nurses must not withhold the whole truth from clients even when it may lead to patient distress.
